heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 17 書證 · 8 … 24
顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 17 書證 · 39 … 1

items.text: Correct your children's speech from infancy, and if a word is mispronounced, count it as your own fault.
items.quote: 吾家兒女，雖在孩稚，便漸督正之；一言訛替，以為己罪矣。 — My own children, even in infancy, I gradually correct their speech; if one word is mispronounced, I count it as my own fault.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 8 勉學 · 10 … 17

items.text: Make the care and support of your parents your constant aim.
items.quote: 子當以養為心 — A son should set his heart on caring for his parents.

items.text: A father should make learning the core of his teaching to his children.
items.quote: 父當以學為教 — A father should make learning his teaching.

items.text: Serve your parents in sickness with all your strength, and let learning refine your filial devotion so that you do not speak or act amiss.
items.quote: 孝為百行之首，猶須學以修飾之 — Filial piety is the foremost of all conducts, yet it still needs to be refined by learning.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 17 書證 · 25 … 38

items.text: Serve your parents-in-law day and night, staying by their side as if you were their own child.
items.quote: 古者，子婦供事舅姑，旦夕在側，與兒女無異 — In ancient times, a daughter-in-law served her parents-in-law, staying by their side morning and evening, no different from their own children.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 1 序致 · 1 … 2

items.text: Warm the bed for your parents in cold weather and cool it in hot weather.
items.quote: 曉夕溫凊 — morning and evening warming and cooling

items.text: Be both stern and kind, so that your children will respect you and become filial.
items.quote: 父母威嚴而有慈，則子女畏慎而生孝矣。 — If parents are dignified yet kind, children will be respectful and filial.

items.text: Train your children; punishment is like medicine for an illness, so do not withhold it out of tenderness.
items.quote: 當以疾病爲諭，安得不用湯藥鍼艾救之哉？ — Consider illness as an analogy; how can one not use medicine and acupuncture to save them?

items.text: Keep some dignity toward your son: do not be overfamiliar, but do not be negligent in your love.
items.quote: 父子之嚴，不可以狎；骨肉之愛，不可以簡。 — Between father and son there must be dignity, not familiarity; love between kin must not be careless.

items.text: Do not personally teach your son the classics; entrust him to a teacher because the texts contain matters unfit for father and son to discuss.
items.quote: 蓋君子之不親教其子也 — a gentleman does not personally teach his son
items.conflict: Deuteronomy 6:6-7 commands parents to teach God's words to their children.

items.text: Love all your children equally; favoritism brings ruin.
items.quote: 有偏寵者，雖欲以厚之，更所以禍之。 — To show favoritism, intending to be generous, actually brings disaster.

items.text: Do not teach your child servile arts merely to please the powerful.
items.quote: 教其鮮卑語及彈琵琶...若由此業，自致卿相，亦不願汝曹爲之。 — Teaching him the Xianbei tongue and lute... even if it leads to high office, I would not have you do it.

items.text: Love your brothers deeply; do not let outsiders or wives weaken that bond.
items.quote: 兄弟者，分形連氣之人也...惟友悌深至，不爲旁人之所移者，免夫！ — Brothers share one body and breath... only deep fraternal love unmoved by outsiders avoids this.

items.text: After your parents die, care for each other like form and shadow.
items.quote: 二親既歿，兄弟相顧，當如形之與影，聲之與響 — When both parents are gone, brothers must care for one another as shadow follows form, echo follows sound.

items.text: Be forbearing with your sisters-in-law and treat each other's children as your own.
items.quote: 若能恕己而行，換子而撫，則此患不生矣。 — If you can exercise forbearance and rear one another's children, this trouble will not arise.

items.text: Serve your elder brother with respect, but do not expect the same love he gives his own children.
items.quote: 人之事兄，不可同於事父，何怨愛弟不及愛子乎？ — Serving an elder brother is not the same as serving a father; why resent that he loves his brother less than his own son?

items.text: Be cautious about taking a second wife; a harsh stepmother can abuse your children.
items.quote: 假繼慘虐孤遺，離閒骨肉，傷心斷腸者，何可勝數。慎之哉！ — A stepmother cruelly mistreating the orphaned, alienating flesh and blood, how many heartbroken cases! Be careful!

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 7 慕賢 · 6 … 9

items.text: Educate your children from an early age in the classics and proper learning.
items.quote: 士大夫子弟，數歲已上，莫不被教 — Every son of a scholar-official, from several sui upward, is taught.

items.text: Serve your parents by anticipating their wishes, speaking gently, working hard to provide good food, and doing it gladly.
items.quote: 先意承顏，怡聲下氣，不憚劬勞，以致甘腝 — anticipate their wishes, speak gently, shrink from no toil, and provide delicious food.

items.text: Encourage your children to model themselves on the accomplished men of old, not only on notable neighbors and kin.
items.quote: 人見鄰里親戚有佳快者，使子弟慕而學之，不知使學古人 — When they see a capable neighbor or kinsman, they have their sons admire and learn from him; they do not think of having them study the ancients.

items.text: Do not become arrogant from a little learning and treat your elders with disrespect.
items.quote: 見人讀數十卷書，便自高大，淩忽長者，輕慢同列 — When he has read a few dozen scrolls, he thinks highly of himself, slights his elders, and treats his equals with contempt.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 8 勉學 · 18 … 30

items.text: In speech and writing, when citing the ancients, you must learn with your eyes; do not trust what you merely hear.
items.quote: 谈说制文，援引古昔，必须眼学，勿信耳受。

items.text: Learn the forms, sounds, and meanings of characters; treat philology as the root of all book learning.
items.quote: 文字者，坟籍根本；小学乃其宗系。

items.text: Do not presume to correct or emend books until you have broadly read; do not make hasty judgments.
items.quote: 观天下书未遍，不得妄下雌黄。

items.text: Study the characters in your own name and those of your kin, and their homophones, so that you are not deceived when asking about them.
items.quote: 凡如此例，不预研检，忽见不识，误以问人，反为无赖所欺，不容易也。

items.text: Do not pretend to learning by hearsay; if you use an allusion or reference, know its source.
items.quote: 道听涂说，强事饰辞，皆耳学之过也。

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 9 文章 · 16 … 1

items.text: Do not touch up your child's essays to raise his reputation; that is a great fault.
items.quote: 治點子弟文章，以為聲價，大弊事也。 — To touch up a son's writings to raise his price is a great fault.

items.text: Mourn your parent sincerely; do not counterfeit grief to gain a name for filial piety.
items.quote: 以巴豆塗臉，遂使成瘡，表哭泣之過。 — Applied croton oil to his face to make sores, feigning excessive weeping.

items.text: Build a good name; it will be a robe and a wall to your descendants.
items.quote: 祖考之嘉名美譽，亦子孫之冕服墻宇也。 — Ancestors' good name and fine repute are the robe and wall of their descendants.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 9 文章 · 1 … 15

items.text: Consult your relatives and friends for their judgment before putting out your writing; do not trust your own heart alone.
items.quote: 先謀親友，得其評裁 — First consult relatives and friends, get their judgment.

items.text: Obey your father's command: do not lightly criticize others' writings.
items.quote: 汝曹必無輕議也 — You all must certainly not lightly discuss or ridicule.

items.text: Admonish him when he goes astray, even to the point of tears.
items.quote: 其妻，明鑒婦人也，泣而諫之 — His wife, a woman of clear discernment, wept and admonished him.

items.text: Take your wife's wise counsel to heart; do not dismiss it out of pride.
items.quote: 才華不為妻子所容 — My talent is not tolerated by my wife.

items.text: When serving your parents, be careful that your words and writings do not bring them sorrow or disrespect.
items.quote: 北面事親，別舅摛渭陽之詠 — When serving parents, if parting from maternal uncle, using the Weiyang poem is a mistake.

items.text: Serve your father with the same reverence you would show your ruler.
items.quote: 資於事父以事君而敬同 — Serving father and serving ruler use the same respect.

items.text: Warn your children against literary arrogance and self-conceit; teach them to be humble.
items.quote: 今世文士，此患彌切 — Modern literary men have this fault even more.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 6 風操 · 27 … 5

items.text: Do not enter the room where your deceased parents lived; let it remain closed out of grief and reverence.
items.quote: 二親旣沒，所居齋寢，子與婦弗忍入焉 — When both parents are dead, the room they lived in, son and daughter-in-law cannot bear to enter.

items.text: With your husband, do not enter the room where his deceased parents lived; let it remain closed out of grief.
items.quote: 二親旣沒，所居齋寢，子與婦弗忍入焉 — When both parents are dead, the room they lived in, son and daughter-in-law cannot bear to enter.

items.text: Preserve your father's books and mother's cups that bear their marks; do not use them but seal them for posterity.
items.quote: 父之遺書，母之杯圈，感其手口之澤，不忍讀用...惟當緘保，以畱後世耳 — Father's books with his notes, mother's cups with her lip prints, because of their touch, one cannot bear to read or use... only seal and preserve them for later generations.

items.text: On the anniversary of a parent's death, refrain from music, receiving guests, and ordinary business.
items.quote: 忌日不樂...故不接外賓，不理眾務耳 — On the death anniversary, do not be merry; therefore do not receive guests or manage business.

items.text: On festival days that fall near a parent's death anniversary, be extra sorrowful and do not feast, listen to music, or go out.
items.quote: 今二親喪亡，偶値伏臘分至之節，及月小晦後，忌之外，所經此日，猶應感慕，異於餘辰，不預飲燕、聞聲樂及行遊也 — Now when both parents are dead, if festival days like the solstices, equinoxes, or month-end besides the death anniversary occur, still be moved with longing, different from other days; do not join in feasting, listening to music, or going out.

items.text: Avoid writing the characters of your father's personal name; use substitutes.
items.quote: 其父名昭，一生不爲照字...凡文與正諱相犯，當自可避 — Their father's name was Zhao; all their lives they did not use the character zhao (照)... In writing, if a character clashes with the true taboo, you should avoid it.

items.text: If your parents are dead, on your birthday do not feast and make merry; instead be sorrowful.
items.quote: 自茲已後，二親若在，每至此日，嘗有酒食之事耳。無教之徒，雖已孤露，其日皆爲供頓，酣暢聲樂，不知有所感傷 — After that, if parents are alive, on this day they have a feast. But untaught people, though orphaned, on that day prepare feasts, drink, make music, and do not know sorrow.

items.text: If your father, grandfather, or uncle is in danger in battle, humble yourself and do not hold music, feasts, or weddings.
items.quote: 父祖伯叔，若在軍陣，貶損自居，不宜奏樂燕會及婚冠吉慶事也 — If father, grandfather, or uncles are in battle, humble yourself and do not have music, feasts, or weddings and cappings.

items.text: When your parent is gravely ill, humble yourself before the physician, weeping and bowing, to entreat his help.
items.quote: 父母疾篤，醫雖賤雖少，則涕泣而拜之，以求哀也 — When parents are gravely ill, though the physician is lowly or young, weep and bow to him to beg for mercy.

items.text: If your father is arrested or accused, humble yourself: go barefoot and unkempt, plead for him before authorities, and resign office if necessary.
items.quote: 梁世被繫劾者，子孫弟姪，皆詣闕三日，露跣陳謝；子孫有官，自陳解職。子則草屩麤衣，蓬頭垢面，周章道路，要候執事，叩頭流血，申訴冤枉 — In Liang times, if someone was arrested, sons, grandsons, and nephews all went to the palace barefoot; if they had office, they resigned. Sons wore straw sandals and coarse clothes, disheveled, waited on officials, knocked heads till bleeding, to plead injustice.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 4 後娶 · 3 … 4

items.text: Do not let partiality make you favor your own children and mistreat your stepchildren; such favoritism breeds resentment and feuds.
items.quote: 異姓寵則父母被怨，繼親虐則兄弟爲讎 — Favoring stepchildren causes parental resentment; mistreating them makes siblings enemies.

items.text: Serve your parents faithfully even when they treat you harshly; do not abandon them, but persist in filial care until they relent.
items.quote: 包日夜號泣，不能去，至被毆杖。 — Xue Bao wept day and night and would not leave, even when beaten.

items.text: In dividing inheritance, yield the better shares to your younger siblings; do not contend for advantages.
items.quote: 奴婢引其老者，田廬取其荒頓者 — He took the old servants and the neglected fields.

items.text: Discipline your children with measured firmness; do not neglect correction, but do not punish unjustly.
items.quote: 笞怒廢於家，則豎子之過立見 — If beating and anger are abolished, children's faults immediately appear.

items.text: Manage the household economy with frugality and generosity: give without extravagance, economize without stinginess.
items.quote: 如能施而不奢，儉而不吝，可矣 — Give without extravagance, be frugal without stinginess.

items.text: Work the land for food, raise mulberry and hemp for clothing, and supply the household's needs by your own labor.
items.quote: 生民之本，要當稼穡而食，桑麻以衣 — The people's foundation: plow for food, grow mulberry for clothing.

items.text: Receive and support impoverished relatives who cannot feed or clothe themselves; share your food with them without resentment.
items.quote: 皆收養之；躬自同之，常無厭色 — He adopted them and shared their gruel without distaste.

items.text: Do not mistreat your daughter-in-law; treat her with the kindness due to your own child.
items.quote: 率寵子壻而虐兒婦 — Dote on sons-in-law, mistreat daughters-in-law.

items.text: Do not reduce the food and clothing of wife and children; provide adequately for all members.
items.quote: 妻子節量，此亦爲家之巨蠹矣 — Stinting wife and children is a great household worm.

items.text: Take charge of the kitchen and clothing; do not meddle in family or state governance, but help your husband where he is lacking.
items.quote: 婦主中饋，惟事酒食衣服之禮耳 — The wife manages provisions and only handles wine, food, and clothing.

items.text: Do not beat or rage at servants; correct them with patience and forbearance.
items.quote: 竟無捶撻 — He never beat the maid.

items.text: Do not abandon or kill a baby girl; she is your own flesh and blood, so raise her as your child.
items.quote: 世人多不舉女，賊行骨肉 — Many do not raise daughters, cruelly killing their own flesh.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 14 誡兵 · 1 … 7

items.text: Remember and keep the family's scholarly heritage; do not seek advancement through arms.
items.quote: 子孫誌之 — Remember it, my sons and grandsons.

items.text: Do not bring ruin on your family by reckless military schemes.
items.quote: 此皆陷身滅族之本也。誡之哉！ — These are the root of ruining oneself and destroying one's clan. Be warned!

items.text: When young, diligently support your parents.
items.quote: 幼少之日，既有供養之勤 — When young, there is the diligent duty of supporting parents.

items.text: When grown, provide for your wife.
items.quote: 成立之年，便增妻孥之累 — When grown, you add the burden of wife and children.

items.text: When grown, provide for your children.
items.quote: 成立之年，便增妻孥之累 — When grown, you add the burden of wife and children.

items.text: Do not devote yourself to seeking immortality, as your father commands.
items.quote: 不願汝曹專精於此 — I do not wish you to devote yourselves to this.

items.text: Be willing to lose your own life to keep your family whole.
items.quote: 喪身以全家 — lose your body to keep the family whole.

items.text: Do not treat lightly the faith to which our family has given its heart.
items.quote: 家世歸心，勿輕慢也 — The family has turned its heart to it; do not treat it lightly.
items.conflict: Worship of any other god is forbidden (Exodus 20:3).

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 19 雜藝 · 10 … 4

items.text: Learn a little medicine well enough to compound simples and rescue your household in emergencies.
items.quote: 微解藥性，小小和合，居家得以救急，亦為勝事 — Understand a little of drug properties, compound simples, at home rescue emergencies—a fine thing.

items.text: Do not seek praise for your music or let it bind you to serve nobles for leftovers; keep it as private refinement.
items.quote: 唯不可令有稱譽，見役勳貴，處之下坐，以取殘杯冷炙之辱 — Only do not let it win you praise, make you serve nobles, sit below, take the shame of cold leftovers.

items.text: Use chess and games only when tired, as relief, but never let them become a constant habit.
items.quote: 圍棋有手談、坐隱之目，頗為雅戲；但令人耽憒，廢喪實多，不可常也 — Go is a refined game, but it makes men absorbed, confused, causing much loss; it must not be constant.

items.text: Bury me simply: wash my body, use common clothes, a modest pine coffin, no grave mound, and mark the plot with a low wall.
items.quote: 沐浴而已，不勞覆魄，殮以常衣...松棺二寸...平地無墳 — Just wash; trouble not to call back the soul; shroud in ordinary clothes... pine coffin two inches... level ground, no mound.

items.text: At the spirit table on new moon, full moon, and mourning anniversaries, set out only plain gruel, water, dried dates; never wine, meat, cakes, or fruit; refuse friends' libations.
items.quote: 靈筵勿設枕幾，朔望祥禫，唯下白粥清水幹棗，不得有酒肉餅果之祭 — At the spirit bier set no pillow or table; on new moon, full moon, and mourning days, offer only white congee, clear water, dried dates; no wine, meat, cakes, fruit.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with Scripture's warning against consulting the dead (Deut 18:11).

items.text: Offer the seasonal sacrifices and the mid-seventh-month Ullambana, but do not kill animals or drain your livelihood.
items.quote: 四時祭祀，周、孔所教...若報罔極之德，霜露之悲，有時齋供，及七月半盂蘭盆，望於汝也 — Seasonal sacrifices are taught by Zhou and Confucius... to repay boundless virtue, at times make vegetarian offerings and mid-seventh-month Ullambana; I look to you.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration and offerings to the dead conflict with Scripture (Luke 16:26; Heb 9:27).

items.text: Make passing on our learning and gaining an honorable name your chief aim; do not cling to my decaying grave and vanish into obscurity.
items.quote: 汝曹宜以傳業揚名為務，不可顧戀朽壤，以取堙沒也 — Make it your aim to pass on the family's learning and gain a name; do not cling to decaying soil and be buried in obscurity.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 16 歸心 · 8 … 7

items.text: Do not abandon your wife when you set up a family.
items.quote: 樹立門戶，不棄妻子 — establish a household, do not abandon wife and children.

items.text: Do not abandon your children when you set up a family.
items.quote: 樹立門戶，不棄妻子 — establish a household, do not abandon wife and children.

items.text: Love your son's wife as your own child; do not revile her or belittle her dowry.
items.quote: 但憐己之子女，不愛己之兒婦 — only love their own children, not love their son's wife.

items.text: Do not revile or insult the parents of your son's wife.
items.quote: 罵辱婦之父母 — rebuke and insult the wife's parents.

items.text: Provide offerings and seek blessings for the spirits of your deceased kin when they appear in dreams asking for food.
items.quote: 世有魂神，示現夢想...求索飲食，征須福佑 — there are souls and spirits that appear in dreams... asking for food and drink, seeking blessings.
items.conflict: The dead do not appear or ask for food; such is demonic deception (Deuteronomy 18:11-12).

items.text: Refrain from taking life, so that your children do not suffer calamity for your sins.
items.quote: 好殺之人，臨死報驗，子孫殃禍 — those who love to kill, at death receive retribution, children and grandchildren suffer calamity.
items.conflict: Each person must bear his own sin; descendants are not punished for a parent's sin (Ezekiel 18:20).

items.text: If you do not become a monk, still keep the precepts and recite the scriptures, to prepare a ford and bridge for the next life.
items.quote: 未能出家；但當兼修戒行，留心誦讀，以為來世津梁 — cannot leave home; but should also practice the precepts, pay attention to recitation, to be a ford and bridge for the next life.
items.conflict: Salvation is by grace through faith in Christ, not by reciting Buddhist scriptures (Ephesians 2:8-9).

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 11 涉務 · 2 … 3

items.text: When kinsmen are in danger or distress, spend family wealth and your own strength to help them without grudging.
items.quote: 親友之迫危難也，家財己力，當無所吝 — When relatives and friends are pressed by danger, one should not begrudge family wealth and personal strength.

items.text: Obey the ancestor's injunction: in office do not rise above two thousand shi.
items.quote: 仕宦不可過二千石 — In office do not exceed two thousand shi.

items.text: Obey the ancestor's injunction: do not marry into powerful families for the sake of their influence.
items.quote: 婚姻勿貪勢家 — In marriage do not covet powerful families.

items.text: Keep the household within moderate limits: no more than twenty servants, ten qing of good land, and a modest store of cash; if you exceed, distribute the surplus; if you fall short, do not seek it by unrighteous means.
items.quote: 奴婢盛多，不可出二十人，良田十頃，蓄財數萬 — Servants should not exceed twenty, good land ten qing, savings several tens of thousands.

items.text: Do not seek office through bribery or improper connections, lest you bring ruin and disgrace upon the whole clan.
items.quote: 以財貨托附外家，諠動女謁…莫不破家 — Relying on wealth and connections to seek office… none but ruined their family.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 6 風操 · 5 … 26

items.text: When naming your son, choose a name that will not be a burden to his descendants; avoid names that are too common or too highly honored.
items.quote: 凡名子者，當爲孫地 — When naming a son, make provision for the grandchildren.

items.text: When speaking of your father's elder brother, call him by his birth order, never 'my'—he is above your father, so do not claim him as your own.
items.quote: 言己世父，以次第稱之，不云家者，以尊於父，不敢家也。 — When speaking of your father's elder brother, call him by his order, not 'my'; because he is above your father, you dare not call him 'my'.

items.text: When referring to another person's grandparents, parents, elder uncles and aunts, add a term of veneration; for younger uncles and aunts, add a term of worth—distinguish the ranks.
items.quote: 稱彼祖父母、世父母、父母及長姑，皆加尊字，自叔父母已下，則加賢字，尊卑之差也。 — When addressing their grandparents, uncles, parents, and elder aunts, add 'venerable'; for younger uncles and aunts, add 'worthy'—this distinguishes high and low.

items.text: At winter solstice or New Year, do not visit a house in mourning; send a letter, or after the festival dress properly and go to express your sympathy.
items.quote: 冬至歲首，不詣喪家；若不修書，則過節束帶以申慰。 — At winter solstice and New Year, do not visit a house in mourning; if you do not send a letter, then after the festival dress properly and go to express sympathy.

items.text: When speaking of your departed ancestors, feel grief and longing; and if you must mention a deceased relative, compose your face, sit straight, and use the proper form for his rank.
items.quote: 言及先人，理當感慕 — When speaking of departed ancestors, one ought to feel grief and longing.

items.text: When your cousin is fatherless, in his presence address his mother as 'aunt'—do not avoid the title.
items.quote: 從父兄弟姊妹已孤，而對其前，呼其母爲伯叔母，此不可避者也。 — When your cousin is fatherless, in his presence call his mother 'aunt'—this is unavoidable.

items.text: In the presence of a brother's orphaned son, do not call him 'brother's son'; say 'nephew' so as not to reopen his grief.
items.quote: 兄弟之子已孤，與他人言，對孤者前，呼爲兄子弟子，頗爲不忍 — When a brother's son is fatherless, and you speak with others in his presence, calling him 'brother's son' is quite painful.

items.text: Do not call your mother's parents by the same name as your father's; always add 'maternal' to keep the distinction.
items.quote: 呼外祖父母與祖父母同，使人爲其不喜聞也。雖質於面，皆當加外以別之。 — Calling maternal grandparents the same as paternal makes people unhappy to hear; even face to face, add 'maternal' to distinguish.

items.text: When a death occurs, do not follow the heterodox books: do not flee the house, draw talismans, light fires, or exorcise spirits; such practices are unfeeling and deserve censure.
items.quote: 子孫逃竄，莫肯在家；畫瓦書符，作諸厭勝；喪出之日，門前然火，戶外列灰，祓送家鬼，章斷注連 — Descendants flee and will not stay home; they draw tiles and write talismans, make various apotropaic devices; on the day of the funeral, they light fires before the gate and spread ashes outside to exorcise household spirits and cut off the 'connection'.

items.text: Treat the personal name of a deceased ancestor as taboo: do not use it; his style name may be used for descendants.
items.quote: 名終則諱之，字乃可以爲孫氏 — After death the personal name is taboo; the style name may be used for descendants.
items.conflict: No biblical requirement to avoid names of the dead; honor is through godly remembrance, not taboo.

heading: 顏氏家訓 Yanshi Jiaxun · Yan Zhitui · 顏氏家訓 18 音辭 · 2 … 9

items.text: Do not hunt birds and beasts for sport.
items.quote: 雖然要輕禽，截狡獸，不願汝輩為之。 — Although it is for taking light birds and cutting down cunning beasts, I do not wish you to do it.

items.text: Do not over-refine calligraphy or pride yourself on it; it leads to servitude and shame.
items.quote: 此藝不須過精。... 慎勿以書自命。 — This art need not be too refined... Be careful not to pride yourself on calligraphy.

items.text: Do not become so skilled in painting that you are used as a common artisan; it brings shame.
items.quote: 向使三賢都不曉畫，直運素業，豈見此恥乎？ — If these three worthies had not known painting, but had pursued their original calling, would they have seen this shame?

items.text: Do not practice divination or yin-yang techniques; they are unreliable and can bring disaster.
items.quote: 凡陰陽之術...驗少妄多。 — All yin-yang arts... few verifications and many absurdities.

items.text: Learn arithmetic as one of the six arts, but do not make it your sole profession.
items.quote: 算術亦是六藝要事...然可以兼明，不可以專業。 — Arithmetic is also an important matter of the six arts... but it may be learned as a secondary knowledge, not as a profession.

items.text: Do not mispronounce your own name, lest your children and grandchildren be entangled in taboos.
items.quote: 非唯音韻舛錯，亦使其兒孫避諱紛紜矣。 — Not only are the sounds wrong, but it causes their sons and grandsons to have many naming taboos.

items.text: Train your sons in correct pronunciation; give them proper tutors and models.
items.quote: 元帝手教諸子侍讀，以此為誡。 — Emperor Yuan personally instructed the tutors of his sons, using this as a warning.

items.text: Study and correct your pronunciation; do not follow erroneous or vulgar readings.
items.quote: 此例甚廣，必須考校。 — Such examples are very numerous; they must be examined and corrected.
